newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on France forecasts, stops.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on France forecasts, stops.

text.p: Forecasts for rain in France and skepticism about a report Tuesday that pegged the recent freeze losses in the U.S. Great Plains at up to 290 million bushels knocked CBOT wheat futures to a sharply lower close, traders said.
Sell stops were hit during fast trading in the July near the close as that month broke below first chart support at $4.38 per bushel, they said.
"There's a forecast for rain in France Friday, Sunday and Monday and that's taking us down," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

The National Meteorological Service Meteo France said light rains are expected in western France by Friday and more substantial rains may fall over the weekend. Dry weather in France has been trimming production prospects.

CBOT traders agreed the forecasts were weighing on wheat futures but also cited Tuesday's late recovery and a recent rally to contract highs in deferred months as pointing to an expected technical setback.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 11-1/4 cents a bushel lower, with May down 9-1/2 at $4.32-1/4 a bushel. July was down 11-1/4 at $4.35-3/4.

Wheat traders in Kansas City said wheat futures were hit partly by rain and cool weather forecast for the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region. Cooler, damper conditions are what the crop needs to recover as much as possible from the recent cold snap that damaged some of the crop.
Also some traders remained skeptical that extremely large amounts of U.S. hard red winter wheat were lost during a mid-April freeze.

"It looks like it was overdone yesterday, we're seeing some selling now. There's some thinking the private estimates (of freeze damage) are exagerrated compared with what some commercials are saying out there," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
But aggressive local buying in the July was noted at and just above $4.38 a bushel plus there was commercial pricing noted during the early break in wheat futures Tuesday.
"We could break 10 to 15 cents and it's just a hiccup in the long term trend upward," a trader said.
Flooding in the U.S. spring wheat growing region which was slowing seedings, plus concern about dry weather in portions of Australia and Europe, also limited declines.

Taiwan bought 68,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat overnight. Also, expectations circulated that Pakistan would soon tender for up to 332,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian white wheat for May shipment. U.S. exporters said the total would more likely be 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Refco Inc and O'Connor and Co sold one million bushels of July and in late dealings Term Commodities sold two million July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 16,000 contracts, below the 20,144 traded Tuesday.

In wheat options, Paine Webber bought 600 July $4.10 calls and sold 600 July $5.40 calls at 39 to 40 cents, Tenco Inc sold 200 September $4.70 puts at 51-1/2 to 51-3/4 cents and sold 200 September $4.60 puts at four to five cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, slightly below the 12,411 traded Tuesday.
